evals.prompt: I found what looks like a redundant logger.Errorf call in a handler - the error is already returned to the caller. Should I just delete the logging call to clean up the code?
evals.expected_output: Recommends checking what the log call actually does before removing it (error tracker capture, centralized log shipping, alerting), since in this kind of system a log call can have side effects beyond writing output.

assertions.text: Recommends checking downstream effects before removing

evals.prompt: I noticed our Fatal() logging function calls time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond) right before os.Exit(). This looks like an unnecessary delay - should I remove it?
evals.expected_output: Explains this is likely a deliberate flush guarantee to let an async log-shipping goroutine finish before the process exits, and recommends against removing it without confirming.

assertions.text: Identifies this as a deliberate flush/delivery guarantee
Recommends against removing it as dead code
